prompt:
Bug: the brute-force ingredient parser splits a multi-word food into a unit and a food.

With the foods "onion" and "green onion" in the group, parsing "1 green onion" with the brute parser (RegisteredParser.brute, parse_one) gives quantity 1, a unit "green" that matches no unit, and the food "onion". The parser already re-joins a wrongly split unit and food, but only when neither of them matched anything. Here the second word alone matches a food, so the join never happens.

Expected, in ABCIngredientParser.find_ingredient_match (used by all parsers):
- When the unit matched no known unit but the food did match, take the unit and food words as parsed, joined with a space ("green onion"). If that is exactly the name, plural name or alias of a known food (after the usual normalization), use that food and drop the unit. "1 green onion" then parses to quantity 1, no unit, food "green onion" and no note; a parsed unit "green" with food "onion" ends as the food "green onion" (an IngredientFood) and unit None.
- In that case a fuzzy match must not replace the food that already matched: a parsed unit "gren" with food "onion" keeps the unit "gren" as parsed (a CreateIngredientUnit) and the matched food "onion", even though "gren onion" is close to "green onion".
- When neither unit nor food matched, the joined name is still fuzzy matched as today. Everything else stays the same: for example, unit "very unique" with food "fresh ginger" keeps both, and unit "cup" with food "gren onion" still gives "Cups" and "green onion".

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/services_tests/ingredient_parser` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: fix: match multi-word foods when the brute parser splits off an unknown unit (#8744)
